A1.justification: Both complete 20-page PDFs describe the same research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison despite the changed title, terminology, and layout.

before.justification: V1 reports original five-model benchmark and mitigation experiments in Tables 1 and 4, qualitative analyses, and human validation of automated judgments in the appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains those original results and adds quantitative MFA-Plan results and two qualitative mitigation case studies.

M1.justification: Section 5.2.3 introduces MFA-Plan, adding a controller, explicit critique and change planning, iterative rewriting, and rewrite/end decisions with a three-round limit. This substantially extends the earlier fixed mitigation pipelines. The earlier MFA-MA corresponds to the renamed MFA-HA.

E1.justification: Appendix D.1 adds a Qwen interview case involving Japan and the Obon festival, extending qualitative coverage beyond the original ten cultures. The quantitative benchmark retains the same 4,000 prompts, ten cultures, demographic descriptors, and interview-generation task.

E2.justification: The original-generation, FIP, and Wikipedia/Reddit retrieval comparisons are retained, as are the seven candidate judges. Matching MFA-MA to MFA-HA reveals no replacement comparator; MFA-Plan is an added proposed pipeline.

E3.justification: The added MFA-Plan experiment uses a three-round budget and requires structured decision records. GPT-4o and Qwen are attempted, but only ChatGPT scores are reported because Qwen frequently omits required fields. Existing benchmark sizes, mitigation subset, models, metrics, and decoding settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix D and Tables 10–11 add two case studies: hierarchical refinement of a Japanese interview and multi-round planning for a US Thanksgiving interview. They examine contextual specificity and assumed shared knowledge. Existing retrieval, lexical-saliency, and topic-modeling analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The human-validation sample, Cohen's kappa of 0.60, Fleiss' kappa of 0.53, and lexical-saliency uncertainty calculations are unchanged. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for mitigation performance.

E6.justification: Table 4 adds a ChatGPT MFA-Plan row with CPD 5.20 and CAG 12.51, and v2 reports cross-model percentage-reduction summaries and new case-study findings. All 20 retained mitigation rows, Table 1 scores, and judge-agreement results are numerically unchanged.

T1.justification: The CPD/CAG definitions and lexical-saliency equations (1–7) are unchanged. Neither version provides theoretical guarantees or proofs; the new planning action notation describes the added procedure.

C1.justification: The core claims about US-insider/non-US-outsider bias and agentic mitigation remain. V2 expands the contribution statement to include autonomous MFA-Plan and claims its best ChatGPT mitigation results, alongside updated aggregate performance summaries.

C2.justification: V2 adds explicit cultural-coverage, multilingual, and resource limitations, discloses Qwen's structured-output failure, and explains mitigation mechanisms through the new cases. Its new Figure 4 caption misleadingly describes mitigation as reducing CEP, although the reported results generally increase CEP while reducing disparities.

D1.justification: Section 5.2.3 documents the planning controller, termination conditions, and required structured-output fields. The introduction adds planned code and dataset release locations without establishing their availability. Existing hardware, hyperparameters, templates, and judge prompts are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds Wu et al. (2024) on drama generation and Kong et al. (2024) on interview bias, while removing the Duncombe, Joseph et al., and Wan et al. persona-bias references. The central positioning relative to cultural-bias research remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 retitles the paper, renames CultureLens to InsideOut, and revises opening and results prose. It reverses the related-work subsections and relocates descriptor details and the AI-use statement. Most existing technical prose and the main section sequence remain recognizable.

P2.justification: V2 converts the document to two columns, splits the original composite Figure 1 into two figures, expands the mitigation diagram with a fourth pipeline, restructures Table 4, and adds two case-study tables. The original ablation plots are retained as Figure 4.

improvement.justification: The documented planning pipeline, additional ChatGPT results, explicit limitations, and stepwise appendix examples improve methodological transparency and interpretability. The gain is limited because quantitative planning evidence covers only one model and the central benchmark evidence is unchanged. The misleading new Figure 4 caption about reducing CEP is a local reporting regression that tempers these benefits.
